wb17894.description: Anderson Dam is a popular destination for a relaxing afternoon of fishing and nature enjoyment. The pond is annually stocked with trout by the Alberta Conservation Association (ACA), enhancing angling opportunities for visitors. The shoreline is lined with willows and Saskatoon shrubs, which offer seasonal berry picking for those exploring the area. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb18007.description: This waterbody has been recently designated as a quality fishery and stocked with rainbow trout.

wb18014.description: This little riverside campground is in Heart River Provincial Recreation Area, 20 km north of High Prairie on Hwy. 749, 8 km west on Hwy. 679 and 12 km north on an access road. Here you can go canoeing or boating from a hand launch. Fish in the many small bays and coves, or explore the adjacent Winagami Wildland Provincial Park, as well as Winagami Lake Provincial Park located about 18 km to the south and east. | Amenities notes: Firepits; handlauch

wb18019.description: This pond is on the north east side of Wetaskiwin. ACA stocks this pond annually with trout, typically before the May long weekend. | Amenities notes: garbage receptacles

wb18020.description: ACA annually stocks this pond with trout, typically before the May long weekend. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb18022.description: The fish pond is located on the south side of Highway 12, just before entering the Town of Castor. It is stocked annually with trout, providing anglers with a reliable fishing opportunity throughout the season.

wb18997.description: Odlum Pond Trail is a 220 kilometer moderately trafficked out back trail located near Kananaskis Improvement, that features beautiful wild flowers and is rated as difficult. The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from March until October Dogs are also able to use this trail but must be kept on leash.

wb19525.description: This lake can only be accessed by ATV or by hiking.

wb19760.description: The park contains a picnic shelter and a pond stocked with trout for fishing . The park has also been designated as an off-leash area for dogs, so park users and their four-legged companions can have fun for the day. | Amenities notes: This waterbody is located in Lac La Biche

wb20258.description: Castaway Trout Pond, located near Viking southeast of Edmonton, is an excellent destination for both beginners and experienced anglers to enjoy fishing. The Alberta Conservation Association (ACA) typically stocks this water body before the May long weekend, ensuring great opportunities for anglers throughout the season.

wb20267.description: This pond may be subject to winterkill.

wb21137.description: Grab your fishing rod and tackle, and take your family fishing at Rotary Park. Fishing is limited to people under the age of 16 years, or those accompanied by one or more people under the age of 16 years. | Amenities notes: sports fields; off-leash dog park; river slide attraction

wb2129.description: Medley River Beach is a fantastic day use beach on the west shores of Cold Lake Like most Cold Lake beaches, the sand is plentiful and this beach is on a spit of land. This is a popular beach in July and August for those seeking a day trip and enjoy some stocked trout fishing. | Amenities notes: waste receptacles

wb21332.description: The pond is located in a remote area and can be difficult to access due to a rough road. Fish are stocked in the upper section of the pond, and aeration is provided by a windmill system to maintain water quality. Nearby campsites are available on a first-come, first-served basis, offering a convenient option for visitors who wish to stay close to the pond.

wb21353.description: Ardmore Pond is a quiet small pond on the north side of the community of Ardmore, this small, but peaceful pond is perfect for a lazy day of shore fishing.

wb22504.description: Riverstone pond located in William Pearce Park.

wb22993.description: ACA stocks this pond annually with trout, typically before the May long weekend. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb22995.description: The Peace Ponds are a great for fly fishing.

wb23292.description: Genesee Heritage Park offers visitors a great spot to have a picnic or spend the day fishing in other fully-stocked fish pond.

wb23293.description: This pond is located in the town. Both ponds are stocked with fish.

wb23789.description: This is a small re-claimed mine pond on Cole Valley Mine site. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb23790.description: This is a small re-claimed mine pond on Cole Valley Mine site. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb23791.description: This is a small re-claimed mine pond on Cole Valley Mine site. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb24236.description: Brazeau Canal is a small pond located along the Brazeau Canal, approximately 50 minutes west of Drayton Valley. The pond has been stocked with walleye fry, offering anglers a unique fishing opportunity in a scenic setting. Fishing access is available at the West Canal Campground, which also provides convenient amenities for visitors. In addition to fishing, the area offers a variety of recreational activities, including powerboating, canoeing, and birdwatching. While Off-Highway Vehicle (OHV) trails are available nearby, OHV use is strictly prohibited within the campground to maintain a safe and peaceful environment. The site is adjacent to Brazeau Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area, making it an excellent destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

wb24312.description: This is a small re-claimed mine pond on Cole Valley Mine site. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb24364.description: The lake is stocked annually by AEP with trout and is aerated (October - April) through ACA's Lake Aeration Program.

wb24702.description: The pond is flooded in the winter, where people can enjoy some outdoor skating. | Amenities notes: also amenities can be located within the town

wb26033.description: Fishing enthusiasts will be intrigued to know that the south lake was stocked with trout and is now managed as a quality stocked trout fishery. | Amenities notes: bench

wb26047.description: This is an accessible fish pond, with a cook shack, benches, fire pits for the perfect day out fishing.

wb26322.description: The Len Thompson Fishing Pond in Lacombe, is a stocked retention pond that provides catch and release recreational fishing opportunities for local residents. Home of the worlds largest lure.

wb26431.description: The pond is located in the town of High Level in the community park. There are baseball diamonds, a disc golf course and an off-leash dog park. Enjoy the day fishing at the day-use area. | Amenities notes: off leash dog park

wb26447.description: This is an urban community pond that can be fished by all ages. A fishing license is not required for anglers under the age of 16. | Amenities notes: Bow habitat station has amenities.

wb26729.description: Kakut Lake is located in northern Alberta and offers a great camping experience. Fish the stocked pond for trout with the possibility of perch being caught. | Amenities notes: community hall.

wb26854.description: This pond is in the south west corner of Fort Saskatchewan's West River's Edge Recreational Area and is maintained and managed by the city of Fort Saskatchewan. This pond is stocked with trout by ACA.

wb318138.description: Camp at the pond in one of the nine sites, and throw your line into the stocked pond.

wb328085.description: ACA annually stocks this 8-ha pond with trout. Permission is not required to access the pond for fishing. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb3476.description: Pond is usually stocked at least three-four times a year due to its popularity.

wb3479.description: This lake is south of highway 16, and has an elevation of 912m.

wb3482.description: There is a paved trail around the pond for easy wheelchair accessibility. Day use areas are well treed. The ponds are stocked 3-4 times in spring and early summer with trout. | Amenities notes: park benches

wb3485.description: Fish Game Pond is a little fishing hole for children located in the community of Rocky Mountain House. | Amenities notes: benches; group

wb3486.description: This small pond surrounded by aspen groves is named after Frank Sibbald, a long time rancher who settled in the area in 1875. It is a perfect place to stop, relax and enjoy the foothills environment. You can walk the easy trail along the shore to cast a line and try a little fishing, or simply sit and enjoy a snack at the picnic area.

wb3494.description: Blood Indian Park Campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis and is open seasonally from April 1 to November 1, with winter camping available outside of these dates. The campground features 300 campsites, including 29 serviced sites, making it suitable for a wide range of camping preferences. During the summer months, guests have access to coin-operated showers and a laundromat. Wi-Fi is available in the main camping area for added convenience. Families can also enjoy the Splash Park, which is open daily from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM throughout the summer season. | Amenities notes: rave sewer drainage

wb3499.description: Chain Lakes Reservoir Campground offers more than 90 serviced and unserviced campsites, providing a comfortable and scenic setting for outdoor enthusiasts. Visitors can enjoy a variety of recreational activities, including swimming, beach relaxation, canoeing, fishing, windsurfing, and sailing, making this lakeside destination ideal for both adventure and leisure.

wb3515.description: This waterfront campground is in Little Bow Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area. This prairie campground is all about the water. Many of the sites back on to the reservoir, and trees provide some shade to fish , canoe, water ski, or swim.

wb3522.description: Day use area with fishing, hiking and picnic area.

wb3523.description: Ice fishing access can be difficult at times due to snow accumulation and drifting.

wb3524.description: Michichi Dam Recreation Area has 18 formal power campsites complete with fire pits and picnic tables. There are also 20 overflow campsites, group camping areas, and camp kitchen facilities. There are coin-operated shower facilities with handicap access. There is an RV water and sewer station available for your convenience. Ice fishing is accessible in the winter, but beware of drifting snow when traveling down to the boat launch.

wb3526.description: It's a great spot to enjoy boating, paddling, windsurfing, fishing, birdwatching, or camping.

wb3534.description: Foot access only all year around (weather permitting). After the September long weekend, the services offered at the campsite are reduced.

wb3536.description: Stafford Reservoir is a reservoir located just 45 miles from Chin; whether you’re spinning, fly fishing or bait casting your chances of getting a bite here. | Amenities notes: walk paths

wb3537.description: Travers Dam campground is in Travers Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area.

wb3899.description: Alford Lake borders the Conservation Education Centre for Excellence, established in 1974 to provide youth-focused wildlife conservation education. The centre offers hands-on programs that immerse students in outdoor experiences, helping them develop essential survival skills and environmental awareness. On the opposite side of the lake, a designated public fishing area is available, complete with a small picnic site—ideal for enjoying a relaxing day by the water.

wb3909.description: Allstones Lake Trail is a moderately trafficked 62-mile backcountry route located near Nordegg. The trail is best accessed between April and October, offering scenic views and a rewarding hike to the lake. Dogs are permitted on the trail but must be kept on a leash at all times to ensure safety and environmental protection.

wb3948.description: This trail is considered challenging and is recommended for experienced hikers only due to its steep and rugged terrain. Those making the climb to the campground are encouraged to bring a fishing rod and take advantage of the opportunity to fish in the nearby waterbody. | Amenities notes: bear boxes for security.

wb395186.description: This pond is north of the town of Lodgepole. This pond has lots of shore fishing opportunities and surrounded by trees.

wb395196.description: ACA annually stocks these ponds with trout, typically before the May long weekend. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb4005.description: Bear Pond Trail is an 18-kilometre out-and-back route accessible via the Iron Creek Mountain Trail, located near Longview. Suitable for hikers of all skill levels, the trail is best used from May through November. Dogs are permitted but must be kept on a leash at all times to ensure safety and environmental protection.

wb4011.description: Beauvais Lake borders the Beauvais Main Campground, offering convenient access to the water for campers. Powered sites 1 through 15 are open year-round, from October 1 to April 30. These quiet, well-treed sites provide a peaceful setting and are located close to the lake, making them ideal for both relaxation and recreation.

wb4014.description: The lake is stocked annually with trout by the Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (EPA) and is aerated from October through April as part of the Alberta Conservation Association’s (ACA) Lake Aeration Program. Access to the lake is available by foot, and only electric-powered motors are permitted to help maintain the tranquility and ecological integrity of the area.

wb4018.description: Located within Castle Provincial Park, Beaver Mines Campground offers a scenic and well-equipped setting for both RV and tent camping. Most campsites are nestled among mature trees, providing privacy and shade, while select sites offer picturesque views of the nearby lake. This peaceful location is ideal for nature enthusiasts seeking a relaxing outdoor experience.

wb4027.description: Use the day use area or beach to swim or fish for stocked trout.

wb4061.description: Birch lake lacks a formal boat launch. Recreational users must carry their watercraft to the shoreline and hand-launch directly from the shore. To preserve the natural environment and ensure a quiet experience for all visitors, gas-powered motors are prohibited. Additionally, overnight camping is not permitted at this location.

wb4159.description: Access to this lake is either via a very long trail via the Sheep River Trail.

wb4161.description: The lake is about 3 km long and has an abundance of pike, perch and walleye Burnstick Lake offers something for everyone, including boating, fishing, water skiing, camping and a picnic area. A small store is available for your convenience.

wb4167.description: The hike to Burstall Lakes is an all-season adventure, with winter being a favorite time for many visitors. The trail is relatively flat and easy, making it ideal for snowshoeing or cross-country skiing. Most of the route winds through forested terrain, but expect stronger winds as you approach the lake where tree cover thins. At the trailhead, you’ll find a large parking lot and an outhouse for convenience. | Amenities notes: The upper and lower lakes helicopter stocked. These lakes have recently been stocked in the fall of 2025.

wb4171.description: Butcher’s Lake is nestled in the Castle Region, approximately 21 kilometers south of Pincher Creek. Known for its crystal-clear waters and stunning natural backdrop, this lake is a popular fishing destination throughout the year. Butcher’s Lake is particularly renowned for its excellent brook trout fishing, with regular stocking programs ensuring healthy fish populations and consistent angling opportunities for visitors. | Amenities notes: The lake features a designated day-use area with basic amenities

wb417477.description: There is currently paved vehicle access to within 100 m of the pond and a paved walking path around the pond's perimeter ACA annually stocks this pond with trout, typically before the May long weekend. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb417505.description: Day use area. Come and try your luck catching one of the stocked trout.

wb417506.description: This newly stocked pond near Red Deer is managed by the Alberta Conservation Association (ACA) and offers convenient access for recreational users. While amenities are currently limited, site development is ongoing and improvements will be added over time. The pond provides a great opportunity for anglers to enjoy trout fishing in a peaceful setting.

wb4208.description: Visitors to the park can enjoy a variety of activities, including swimming, canoeing, and trout fishing. The park offers full-service campsites along with convenient amenities such as a laundromat, concession, showers, and washrooms. For recreation, guests can take advantage of ball diamonds, a sand volleyball court, a rugged nine-hole golf course, and multiple playgrounds, making it an ideal destination for families and outdoor enthusiasts. | Amenities notes: golf course nearby

wb4231.description: Cavan Lake Recreational Campground offers 78 campsites, including 60 sites equipped with 30-amp power. Each site features a fire pit, and complimentary firewood is provided for campers. The campground includes amenities such as a playground and horseshoe pits, making it suitable for family recreation. Both campers and anglers can take advantage of the day-use area or reserve group campsites for larger gatherings.

wb4252.description: Chatwin Lake was stocked with trout in the spring of 2020 after many years without fish. The lake boarders the Bonnyville golf course and private residences. The staging area is gravel, with a crude boat launch and smaller boats are recommended.

wb4261.description: Chickakoo Lake Recreation Area is a scenic mix of woods and lakes that attracts a diversity of birds and other wildlife such as moose, dear, beavers and more. The 480 acres of woodland and over 14 km of trails are a popular destination for hikers, cyclists and horseback riders in summer and are groomed for cross country skiers in winter.

wb4265.description: Chin Reservoir is a large, long reservoir where boating, water skiing and fishing are popular. There are only amenities at the camping area which include a boat launch, swimming area and outhouses.

wb4318.description: Formerly called Jeanette, then Lost and now, officially, Commonwealth. Trail Start: Hwy 742 (Smith-Dorrien/Spray Trail) Turn west onto Mt Shark Road In 1 km turn left onto a side road and park a little way in.

wb4340.description: This a popular winter fishing destination. There is a public boat launch available, with a day use area. | Amenities notes: Serviced and un-serviced sites

wb4351.description: This a popular winter fishing destination. There is a public boat launch available, with a day use area. This waterbody has been recently stocked with walleye fry.

wb4374.description: This large, deep, natural lake lies just east of the Continental Divide along Alberta Highway 3 There is a vast parking area at the west end of the lake, a necessary amenity when winter blizzards close the mountain pass. The parking area includes a boat launch where ice fishermen skid their huts onto the ice

wb4426.description: Boat access to the lake is challenging and use the trail at your own risk. | Amenities notes: no open fires; foot access only.

wb4446.description: Sites in this prairie campground are suitable for RVs and tents and most have power. There are many amenities here including a playground, small campground store, toilets, and showers. This park is a great getaway for families who want to devote time to spending time together and fishing for trout. | Amenities notes: life jacket loaner station

wb4458.description: Doleberg Lake campground borders the lake. This campground is a self-registration campground with twelve sites with lots of natural trees. This is a great place to relax a fish for stocked trout.

wb4460.description: This waterbody is stocked by EPA with trout and is aerated during the winter months.

wb4488.description: Dunn Lake is situated east of Petite Lake, and northeast of Jarvis Creek.

wb4495.description: Access found on the Ya Ha Tinda Road or the forestry trunk road through James Pass. Both routes provide direct access to the lake and accommodate horseback and foot travel, with limited ATV/UTV access permitted. Seasonal timing restrictions apply to ATV and UTV use on certain trail segments.

wb4505.description: Electric motors only. There are rocks around the shore making it easy to access the reservoir, fly fishing is preferable.

wb4532.description: A great brook trout destination located 32km north of McLeod Lake.

wb4535.description: The park is off the beaten path, but once you find it, you'll be rewarded with a chain of 5 small lakes and about 7 km of trails to explore. You can fish for stocked trout, canoe, or take an electric powered boat on the lakes and view the hoodoos on the Wild Sculpture Trail.

wb4539.description: A boat launch and day use area are available for day users. Overnight camping and campfires are prohibited.

wb4562.description: Fairfax Lake Provincial Recreation Area has 27 spacious and private sites near the shores of Fairfax Lake. It is ideal for fishing, canoeing , and hiking trails are available in the surrounding area.

wb4571.description: Fickle Lake Campground has 36 sites for both RVs and tents, including lovely campsites with lakeside views. The lots are surrounded by natural spruce forest and allow easy access to the lake, boat launch, dock and shoreline. Although the campground is closed during the winter, the road to the lake and parking lot is still maintained allowing easy access for ice fishing.

wb4614.description: It is encourage to hike or bike up to Fortress Lake up the road access to the trail head. Moterized vehicles access is restricted at this time. Ths is a low intensity hike. The estimated time is 3.4 to 4 hours with a total length of 8.9km with an elevation gain of 559m. To access the hiking trails, you can start from the trailhead located at the Sunwapta Falls parking lot. This is situated along the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) in Jasper National Park. From there, follow the signs and directions to reach the trail leading to your destination.

wb4642.description: Galatea Lakes Hike is a 169 kilometer back trail located near Kananaskis Improvement. The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from May until October. Dogs are also able to use this trail but must be kept on leash.

wb4697.description: Goldeye Lake Campground is located in Goldeye Lake Provincial Recreation Area. There are over 40 un-serviced sites, most surrounded by aspen and spruce trees. Canoe, swim or fish in the stocked lake, or walk the loop trail around it.

wb4708.description: Goose Lake offers camping and fishing. This waterbody has been recently stocked with walleye fry.

wb4725.description: Grande Cache Lake has 8 day use sites that include picnic tables and fire pits. Fire wood is available and has one handicap accessible outhouse facility. Grande Cache Lake has a developed beach area with a playground. For the fishing enthusiasts, there is a boat dock, boat launch, and a fish cleaning station.

wb4794.description: Hasse Lake Recreation area provides a day-use area with walking trails, beach, playground and a picnic shelter. There is a primitive boat launch area with a floating dock east of the main parking area. The shoreline is soft and weedy, but a fishing pier has been installed to increase angling opportunities.

wb4837.description: This lake is one of our helicopter stocked lakes. The lower lake was stocked in the fall of 2025 with 1,200 cutthroat trout. Hogarth Lakes Trail is a scenic 4.2-kilometer loop near Kananaskis Improvement District that features beautiful lakes and is suitable for all skill levels. The trail is best enjoyed from March through October and is dog-friendly, provided pets are kept on a leash.

wb4854.description: Absolutely stunning and well worth the days effort. You will have to cross the Highwood River so expect to get your feet wet. The Alberta - British Columbia boundary runs along the mountains ridge.

wb4888.description: The route to Ice Lake includes numerous river crossings and significant elevation gain. The trail is well-marked along the Panther River Trail, with clear signage at intersections. The round trip from the staging area typically requires 10–12 hours, with the final two hours involving steep elevation gain.

wb4909.description: This campground is in Island Lake Provincial Recreation Area. It has 40 sites which are suited to RVs. This campground offers close access to lakes for canoeing, sailing, boating, fishing for stocked trout or windsurfing.

wb4920.description: The road leading to the campground is paved except for 2km of gravel road at the entrance. Two of the five of the campsites are located on the lake.

wb4935.description: Jane lake is one of our helicopter stocked lakes, which is stocked every three years. The lake was stocked with 1,800 rainbow trout in 2025. The next stocking will happen in 2028.Jane Lake and its surrounding wilderness offer a truly remote and breathtaking escape. A network of scenic trails encircles the lake, providing opportunities for hiking, biking, and camping. These trails have been upgraded and expanded for a safer and more enjoyable experience. The former 4x4 access road has been transformed into a dedicated hiking and biking route, making it easier than ever to reach the lake and explore its natural beauty.

wb4944.description: Jessie is one of our helicopter stocked lakes. It was stocked in the fall of 2025 with 3,500 rainbow trout.Jesse Lake is located approximately 45 km from Swan Hills via off-road trails. Alternatively, you can travel 26 km from Swan Hills to the staging area (4-wheel drive recommended), then continue another 16 km on off-road trails to reach the lake. A 4-wheel drive vehicle is strongly recommended for lake access.

wb4977.description: Kehiwin Cree Nation is operating the Kehiwin Provincial Recreation Area, 28 km east of St. Paul on Hwy. 29, and 7 km north on Hwy. 41. Cozy little campground that offers basic facilities and access with canoe or boat on Kehiwin Lake. | Amenities notes: firepits

wb4978.description: This waterbody has been recently stocked with walleye fry.

wb5002.description: Kinky Lake Campground is found in Wildhorse Lake Provincial Recreation Area, with close lake access. Enjoy the scenic mountain views while fishing for trout. Non-motorized or electric-powered boats only.

wb5029.description: Landslide Lake is a 290km lightly trafficked out and back trail located near Improvement District No 9, Alberta, Canada that offers the chance to see wildlife and is only recommended for very experienced adventurers The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from July until October.

wb5050.description: ACA maintains a fishing access and boat launch is off highway 507. | Amenities notes: no open fires; garbage cans; sanitary receptacles.

wb5074.description: Lillian Lake Backcountry Campground is in Spray Valley Provincial Park. The closest access is at Galatea Day Use Area, 42 km south of Hwy 1 on Hwy 40. It is 63 km from the trailhead via Galatea Creek Trail Camp. There are group fire pits, pit/vault toilets, secure food storage lockers, and raised tent platforms. Note: While there are group fire pits available, firewood is not provided at this site. Please note that it is illegal to remove, deface, injure or destroy trees and using dead wood lying on the ground for firewood is also prohibited. | Amenities notes: bear proof storage containers

wb5078.description: The Lily Lake Trail, located only 25 minutes out of Slave Lake. Beginning at Marten Mountain Viewpoint, this trail descends 28 km to the beautiful Lily Lake.

wb5093.description: Access is very poor for launching larger watercrafts. Parking is close to lake so you may carry your hand launch type watercraft to the waters edge.

wb5149.description: Park in the Lineham Creek recreation area parking lot 134kms west of Calgary located on Highwood Trail #40 highway. Note: Highway #40 is closed at the Upper Lakes and Highwood House Junction from Dec 1st to June 14th for wildlife preservation.

wb5158.description: Lost Guide Lake has an elevation of 2172 metres.

wb5223.description: Access to Margaret Lake is via the Forestry Trunk Road, continuing onto Waiparous Valley Road, which is very rough. The road terminates at a cutline, and the lake is accessible by ATV or UTV. The route leads directly to the lake, with an easy walk from the parking area to the waterbody. Travel time varies depending on road and trail conditions.

wb5232.description: This lake is helicopter stocked and is more accessible with ATV's.

wb5245.description: Mary Gregg Lake is a popular fishing lake for local fishermen.

wb5253.description: Maude Lake is located almost on top North Kananaskis Pass. It's accessed via the Turbine Canyon trail. The Turbine backcountry campground which is only about 2kms away.

wb5275.description: There are about 100 sites suitable for RVs and tents. Camp on the prairies near the lakeside where you can escape the summer heat. Sailing, wind surfing, water skiing, canoeing and fishing are popular activities in and around the waterbody. | Amenities notes: wind surfing

wb5286.description: Carson-Pegasus Provincial Park at McLeod Lake includes a campground featuring 182 campsites, day use sites, and a group use site, and offers winter camping. Other recreational activities at the provincial park and lake include bird-watching, canoeing/kayaking, cross-country skiing, fishing, hiking, horseshoes, ice fishing, power boating, swimming. | Amenities notes: life jacket loaner station; horse shoe pits

wb5324.description: There is a boat launch, and the lake is stocked annually by AEP with trout and is aerated in winter through ACA’s Lake Aeration Program.

wb5336.description: This waterbody has been recently stocked with walleye fry. | Amenities notes: group use

wb5348.description: There is a small campground at the waterbody with walk-in tent sites. There is a pier where you can hand launch a canoe or electric powered boat.

wb5360.description: The campground is located on the north and northeast side of the lake, while the day-use area and group camping is located on the south side of the lake. | Amenities notes: change house

wb5387.description: Muir Lake is an easily accessible quality stocked fishery. Muir Lake features seasonal closures, bait ban and reduced harvest regulations. Seasonal restrictions apply. Check the local regulations before heading out to the lake. | Amenities notes: Basic amenities.

wb5407.description: Enjoy the day fishing the lake, fish from shore or from a boat. The Max boat speed on the lake is 12km/hr.

wb5434.description: This waterbody has been recently stocked with walleye fry.

wb5466.description: A small campground found in Obed Lake Provincial Park. A great spot to launch a boat and fish for trout.

wb5476.description: Wildlife viewing and canoeing are popular activities at this provincial recreation area.

wb5504.description: The well-spaced sites are suitable for tents and RVs and natural poplar forest provides privacy. Relax and spend lazy days fishing from your boat, canoe or shore. | Amenities notes: viewpoints

wb5513.description: The mountains of Waterton National Park that lie 4 km to the southwest provide a dramatic background for the lake.

wb5538.description: This lake often winter kills. Maximum boat speed 12km/h.

wb5555.description: Peppers Lake Campground is located in Peppers Lake Provincial Recreation Area. Go fishing or tour the shoreline by canoe or electric powered boat.

wb5565.description: The Petite Lake Campground is a small campground located adjacent to Petite Lake There are ATV trails in the area, and it is popular for base camping during the hunting season. Electric motors only. | Amenities notes: Located in the glacial cascades natural area - camping adjacent to waterbody.

wb5568.description: This lake is located just west of Coleman near the BC border.

wb5569.description: This scenic little foothills lake is suited to canoeing, fishing and boating with electric powered motors. There are about 20 sites, most of which are open to each other and face the lake. They are suited for both RVs and tents. | Amenities notes: refuse containers

wb5572.description: Electric motor or hand launch boats allowed on the lake.

wb5581.description: Pinehurst Lake and campground is located in Lakeland Provincial Recreation Area, 17 km south of Lac La Biche on Hwy. 36, 5km east on Hwy. 55, 3km north on Range Rd. 132, 19 km east on Township Rd. 652, and 7km north on access road. Pinehurst is a favourite destination for local anglers, and has a staging area outside of the campsite for OHV use for the trail network throughout Lakeland PRA. | Amenities notes: firepits; lifejacket loaner station

wb5646.description: Camping area with serviced sites and a newly build boat launch.

wb5649.description: This is a monderate trail difficulty, with a distance of 7.8km round trip, with an elevation gain of 300m. The trailhead is conveniently located adjacent to the Upper Kananaskis Lake parking lot. The route offers scenic views of Upper Kananaskis Lake, a picturesque waterfall, and sections of old-growth forest. Rawson Lake provides an excellent opportunity for hikers seeking a moderate challenge combined with stunning natural landscapes.

wb5661.description: This is a large spring-fed lake in Cypress Hills Provincial Park.

wb5667.description: There are several different ways to access the lake, including trail heads at Buller Mountain Day Use, Galatea Day Use, and Ribbon Creek Day Use. Note that there is a very steep section of trail with chains to aid climbing between Ribbon Falls and Ribbon Lake Ribbon Lake is a gem tucked away in the heart of Spray Valley. Enjoy the peace and tranquility at this site Here there are tent pads, group fire pits, pit/vault toilets, and secure food storage lockers . | Amenities notes: 10 storage lockers

wb6921.description: Visitors to Brazeau Reservoir can enjoy a wide range of recreational activities, including fishing, powerboating, canoeing, and birdwatching. While Off-Highway Vehicle (OHV) trails are available nearby, OHV use is strictly prohibited within the campground to ensure a safe and peaceful environment. The reservoir is located approximately 50 minutes west of Drayton Valley, adjacent to Brazeau Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area. Fishing access is available at the West Canal Campground, providing convenient opportunities for anglers to enjoy this scenic destination.

wb6923.description: This well-appointed campground offers 21 sites suitable for both RVs and tents, with the option to gather with friends at one of the designated group sites. Most campsites are well-treed, providing privacy and shade, while several are located along a long, winding lake, offering scenic waterfront views. At the campground entrance, visitors will find a concession building equipped with flush toilets, showers, and firewood. A variety of concession items are also available for purchase, adding convenience to your stay.
